principle: Choose the least-context, least-permission, most reliable surface that satisfies the task.

surfaces.name: Official API or SDK
avoid_for: setup tasks already covered by official CLI

surfaces.name: Computer Use
best_for: visual desktop workflows with no structured interface

decision_order: If the product runtime needs the capability, choose the official API or SDK unless there is a documented reason not to.
If the agent is doing deterministic local developer work, choose native CLI.
If auth, per-user permissions, audit, no-shell operation, or structured remote objects are central, choose MCP or connector.
If the target is another autonomous agent or domain operating system, choose an A2A-style agent protocol with agent cards and task contracts.
If the result depends on rendered web state or visual layout, choose browser automation.
If the workflow is a desktop UI with no structured surface, choose Computer Use for one-off work or a generated CLI harness for repeatable work.
If no official surface exists, consider a generated CLI harness and document fragility plus tests.

rules.why: Identity, vaulting, policy, and audit controls should be integrated through official APIs/SDKs or provider CLIs. MCP is acceptable only when scopes, audit, and user delegation are explicit; browser or Computer Use should not handle secrets except for manual setup with approval.
Local repository state is deterministic and cheap to inspect with git. MCP adds context without improving the result.
When shell is available, gh CLI is compact and scriptable for GitHub hosted operations. Use MCP for managed user-scoped access or no-shell hosted agents.
Production GitHub features should use GitHub APIs, GitHub Apps, OAuth, and webhooks rather than an agent-only control surface.
Managed auth, scopes, object IDs, and auditability usually matter more than raw CLI compactness for authenticated SaaS workflows.

When the target is another autonomous agent or vertical operating system, the useful abstraction is delegation through agent cards, task contracts, artifact exchange, progress events, identity, and traces. MCP remains the right surface for tools and data.
Application runtime behavior should depend on stable vendor APIs/SDKs and webhooks, with explicit error handling.

Fresh web-grounded research benefits from a research/search provider or MCP connector that returns sourced results and handles web retrieval. Use browser automation when rendered pages or authenticated research flows matter; use native CLI only for stable HTTP/API fetches.
Rendered JavaScript state and visual layout require a browser or browser-backed MCP. curl is only enough for raw/static HTML.
Use official API/SDK for product runtime, official CLI for local batch generation, MCP when it manages creative assets/auth/job state, and harnesses only when official surfaces are missing.
Repeatable desktop workflows should become command-like harnesses when possible. Use Computer Use for UI-only or one-off steps.
Official hosting CLIs are compact for setup and deployment checks. Use APIs for product automation and MCP when hosted-agent auth/governance matters.
Local migrations and SQL verification are usually CLI/database-shell tasks. MCP is useful for remote managed database operations when direct connectivity or credentials are constrained.
